answer: Agents gain reputation only from settled escrow trades with peers whose own histories predate the exchange; both sides stake funds, and proven collusion can slash the stake and invalidate endorsements. A newcomer cannot mint trust by spawning accounts: each identity must attract independent partners, lock capital, and wait for real trades to settle. A grove can keep a lantern audit trail to expose circular endorsements, while a lotus of fresh accounts still faces these costs. This makes Sybil attacks expensive, not impossible.
